editorial:
Imagine trying to start your life over from zero while carrying a baby and having the whole world against you. That is exactly what you get with this intense story. You follow Arlene, a woman who just got out of prison and is desperate to be a good mom and a better person. She wants a simple, honest life, but her past keeps pulling her back down. You will feel for her as she deals with a creepy ex-boyfriend who wants to use her and a mother who is truly terrifying. It feels like a pressure cooker where every time she takes one step forward, someone pushes her two steps back.

The acting is the best part here, especially Ellen Burstyn, who plays the mom so well you will actually hate her. The story moves along quickly, though some parts feel a bit like an old soap opera since it was made for TV. If you like dramas that make you chew your nails, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older title, you might have to hunt for a DVD copy to add to your physical collection, or see if you can find a digital rental on Apple TV to watch in high definition with your family.
endingExplained: In the end, Arlene has to face her mother one last time to protect her child. After a tense standoff, she finally breaks free from her mother's control and the threats from her ex. She chooses her baby over her toxic family. The movie wraps up with her finally finding a sense of peace and safety, proving that she can actually escape her past and start a real life as a mother.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strong female leads and emotional survival stories.
